title: English
description: ICSE Class IX English: functional grammar, composition, letter, notice and email, comprehension with summary, and the prescribed Treasure Chest prose and poetry for Class IX with Julius Caesar Acts I and II.

syllabusBaselines.source: BoardPrep repository data file (data/icseEnglish.ts), recorded as based on the CISCE ICSE Examination Year 2027 English syllabus and Appendix I.
syllabusBaselines.note: Copied from the repository baseline; the literature titles it lists were re-checked in this run against the reproduced Appendix I (2027 and 2028) and found to be Class X texts, not Class IX texts — see the 2028 baseline entry and the continuation ledger for the reconciliation record.

syllabusBaselines.source: CISCE ICSE Appendix I (Examination Year 2028 and 2027) and the ICSE English (01) syllabus as reproduced by Scribd, corroborated by Shaalaa, Oswal Publishers and Jagran Josh (cisce.org returned 403). Both Appendix reproductions give the same Class IX list.
syllabusBaselines.note: Class IX prescribes Treasure Chest: five prose stories (Bonku Babu’s Friend, Oliver Asks for More, The Model Millionaire, The Home-coming, The Boy who Broke the Bank), five poems (The Night Mail, Skimbleshanks: The Railway Cat, I Remember, I Remember, A Doctor’s Journal Entry for August 6, 1945, A Work of Artifice) and Julius Caesar Acts I and II. Paper 1 requires a composition of about 300-350 words, a letter from a choice of two subjects, a notice and an email on the same given situation, an unseen passage of about 500 words with vocabulary, short answers and a summary, and functional grammar covering prepositions, conjunctions, verbs and sentence structure. The ten titles that were published here before this run (five prose, five poems) are Class X prescriptions; on 2026-10-25, after the placement evidence was documented in the continuation ledger (Phase XIII), their chapter files were relocated intact to class-10/english and published there, leaving Class IX with exactly the prescribed five prose stories and five poems. This subject now publishes 21 chapters: the ten Treasure Chest texts, Julius Caesar Acts I-II, and the Paper 1 language work.

sections.title: English Language
sections.description: Grammar, composition and comprehension skills, with worked examples and practice.

chapters.title: Tenses
chapters.blurb: Time and aspect: choosing the right tense form and avoiding the classic errors.

chapters.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
chapters.blurb: Making verbs agree with the true subject, including tricky cases.

chapters.title: Active and Passive Voice
chapters.blurb: Converting between voices across tenses without changing meaning.

chapters.title: Direct and Indirect Speech
chapters.blurb: Reporting statements, questions and commands with the correct changes.

chapters.title: Prepositions
chapters.blurb: Prepositions of time and place, and fixed word-preposition pairs.

chapters.title: Sentence Structure and Conjunctions
chapters.blurb: Correct sentence structure and the conjunctions that join clauses, as the functional grammar section names.

chapters.title: Essay Writing
chapters.blurb: Planning and writing a clear, well-organised composition.

chapters.title: Letter Writing
chapters.blurb: Formal and informal letters: layout, tone and content.

chapters.title: Notice and Email Writing
chapters.blurb: The prescribed pair: a notice and an email built on the same given situation.

chapters.title: Comprehension Skills
chapters.blurb: Reading closely, answering precisely, inference, vocabulary in context and summary.
